project.name: AgenticAI_Chatbot_Using_RAG
project.description: A free-tier chatbot with streaming answers, hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vectors + reranking), web search, persistent chat history, and an automatic model fallback chain across Groq and Google Gemini. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: mcp_server.py
nodes.summary: Optional stdio MCP server that exposes document search, web search, GitHub connect, and the full chat pipeline to MCP clients.
nodes.languageNotes: Tools are registered on MCPServer and resolve a lazily built ServiceContainer inside the server event loop.

nodes.name: routes.py
nodes.summary: FastAPI router of thin HTTP handlers for chat streaming, sessions, uploads, GitHub, retrieval, and web search.
nodes.languageNotes: Handlers stay thin: FastAPI Depends injects services from the container, and POST /chat/stream serializes pipeline events as SSE.

nodes.name: search_client.py
nodes.summary: Async HTTP clients for Tavily and Serper web search, each with a pooled client and one retry on transient failures.

nodes.name: container.py
nodes.summary: Composition root that constructs every service once, wires constructor dependencies, and exposes FastAPI Depends getters.
nodes.languageNotes: An overrides dict lets tests and the MCP server swap embedders, the LLM client, or other collaborators without reading the environment.

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: FastAPI application factory that configures CORS, mounts the SPA, and owns container startup and shutdown.
nodes.languageNotes: When launched as a script, the module rewrites sys.path so the backend package stays importable and local folders are not treated as top-level modules.

nodes.name: api.py
nodes.summary: Pydantic request and response schemas for sessions, chat, uploads, retrieval, search, GitHub, and health.

nodes.name: artifact.py
nodes.summary: Validates a structured download document and renders it to Markdown, text, Excel, Word, or PDF only when a file is requested.
nodes.languageNotes: File bytes are produced at download time from one validated block document and are not stored on disk.

nodes.name: chat_service.py
nodes.summary: Chat pipeline that routes a turn, checks the semantic cache, retrieves and searches in parallel, then streams a model answer with failover.

nodes.name: search_service.py
nodes.summary: Web search policy with TTL caching, a hard deadline, Tavily-to-Serper fallback, and parallel sub-queries for research mode.

nodes.name: cache.py
nodes.summary: Thread-safe in-process caches: a bounded TTL LRU cache and a per-scope cosine similarity cache of previous answers.
nodes.languageNotes: SemanticCache stores L2-normalized embeddings and only returns a hit inside the same scope tuple, so answers do not leak across users or a changed index.

nodes.name: sse.py
nodes.summary: Encodes a pipeline event dict as one Server-Sent Events frame with an event name and JSON data.

nodes.name: test_api.py
nodes.summary: Offline HTTP tests that exercise every API route, the SSE chat contract, uploads, search fallback, and rate limits.

nodes.name: test_live.py
nodes.summary: Opt-in live tests that measure real model streaming, hybrid retrieval quality, and Tavily latency against provider keys.

nodes.name: web_client.py
nodes.summary: SSRF-safe HTTP client that downloads HTML and text pages for URL ingestion, re-validating every redirect and rejecting oversized responses.
nodes.languageNotes: httpx is created with follow_redirects disabled so each Location hop can be joined and checked before the next GET.

nodes.name: WebPageClient
nodes.summary: Blocking page fetcher that accepts an optional private-URL override and a request timeout, then downloads text-like responses.

nodes.name: fetch_html
nodes.summary: GETs a URL in a manual redirect loop, checks each hop with the SSRF guard, filters content types, and stops if the body exceeds 5 MB.

nodes.name: parser.py
nodes.summary: Converts uploaded documents and web pages into page records of text plus metadata, covering PDF, Office, CSV, Excel, HTML, JSON, images, and plain text.
nodes.languageNotes: Optional format libraries are imported inside each handler. PDF text tries pdfium, then pdfplumber, then PyPDF2, and OCRs pages that have almost no text layer.

nodes.name: DocumentParser
nodes.summary: Dispatches files by extension and URLs through article extraction, returning chunked page dicts ready for indexing.

nodes.name: parse_file
nodes.summary: Routes a saved upload to the handler for its extension and rejects types outside the supported document and image sets.

nodes.name: parse_url
nodes.summary: Fetches a page, extracts article text, and splits it into roughly 1200-character chunks tagged with the parser name and source URL.

nodes.name: _extract_article
nodes.summary: Pulls readable article text with trafilatura and falls back to BeautifulSoup after dropping script, style, and navigation tags.

nodes.name: _parse_pdf
nodes.summary: Reads a PDF text layer with the first successful parser, then OCRs pages that were nearly blank and returns pages in order.

nodes.name: _pdf_pdfium
nodes.summary: Extracts per-page text with pypdfium2, capping the document at 1000 pages and recording pages below the minimum character count as OCR candidates.

nodes.name: _pdf_pdfplumber
nodes.summary: Fallback PDF reader that uses pdfplumber, including table text, and flags pages that are too short for the text layer.

nodes.name: _pdf_pypdf2
nodes.summary: Last-resort PDF text extraction with PyPDF2, using the same page cap and blank-page detection as the faster readers.

nodes.name: _ocr_pdf_pages
nodes.summary: Renders up to 30 sparse PDF pages and runs them through the shared OCR engine, returning nothing when OCR is unavailable.

nodes.name: _parse_image
nodes.summary: OCRs a raster image after converting it to RGB and downscaling the long side, raising a parse error when no text is found.

nodes.name: _parse_docx
nodes.summary: Reads a Word document into sections split on headings and appends table rows as tab-separated text.

nodes.name: _parse_csv
nodes.summary: Loads a CSV into a column summary page plus 50-row data pages that repeat the header on each block.

nodes.name: _parse_excel
nodes.summary: Parses each Excel sheet with pandas into a summary page and 50-row CSV blocks, covering both xlsx and xls.

nodes.name: _paginate_text
nodes.summary: Groups blank-line-separated sections into pages of about 800 characters and stamps each page with the parser name.

nodes.name: _parse_json
nodes.summary: Pretty-prints valid JSON and packs the lines into pages of about 800 characters, rejecting malformed input.

nodes.name: _parse_rtf
nodes.summary: Converts RTF to plain text with striprtf and paginates the result, reporting a clear error when the extra is missing.

nodes.name: _parse_odt
nodes.summary: Reads content.xml from an ODT zip with entity resolution disabled and collects heading and paragraph text.

nodes.name: _parse_pptx
nodes.summary: Extracts one page per slide from shape text, tables, and speaker notes, skipping slides that have no readable text.

nodes.name: _pptx_shape_text
nodes.summary: Walks grouped PowerPoint shapes and appends text-frame and table-cell content in reading order.

nodes.name: _split_into_chunks
nodes.summary: Splits article text on paragraph boundaries into chunks near a target size, keeping a short remainder as its own chunk.

nodes.name: _decode
nodes.summary: Decodes raw text bytes as UTF-8, UTF-16, or cp1252, then charset-normalizer, and always returns a string.

nodes.name: _get_ocr
nodes.summary: Lazily builds one shared RapidOCR engine under a lock and remembers a failed import so later calls stay cheap.

nodes.name: ocr_available
nodes.summary: Reports whether the shared OCR engine could be constructed on this process.

nodes.name: _limit_side
nodes.summary: Downscales an image so its longest side is at most 2000 pixels before OCR.

nodes.name: _ocr_array
nodes.summary: Runs the ONNX OCR engine on an RGB array and joins recognized boxes into lines in reading order.

nodes.name: net.py
nodes.summary: SSRF guard that allows only http(s) URLs whose resolved addresses are public.
nodes.languageNotes: The hostname is resolved with getaddrinfo and each result is classified with ipaddress so a public name that points at a private address is rejected.

nodes.name: UnsafeURLError
nodes.summary: Raised when a URL is not http(s), cannot be resolved, or points at a non-public address.

nodes.name: assert_public_url
nodes.summary: Requires an http(s) URL with a hostname and, unless private URLs are allowed, rejects addresses that are private, loopback, link-local, reserved, multicast, or unspecified.

nodes.summary: Defines the shared @keyframes, motion utility classes, skeleton and progress treatments, and the dashboard and intro motion pack. A reduced-motion block at the end turns continuous animation off for the rest of the UI.

nodes.summary: Styles the chat UI component set—buttons, inputs, session list, messages, citations, code blocks, composer, dialogs, menus, welcome screen, and sidebar controls—using design tokens from main.css.

nodes.summary: Styles the AI Assistant Pro introduction page, scoped to .intro and html[data-view], including the sticky header, hero copy, product preview, and feature grid, with tablet and mobile breakpoints.

nodes.name: main.css
nodes.summary: Design-token source of truth for spacing, type, motion, z-index, and light and dark color schemes, plus reset, layout grid, typography, scrollbar, focus ring, and skip-link primitives.

nodes.name: syntax.css
nodes.summary: Maps highlight.js token classes to --syn-* color tokens so light and dark themes share one syntax stylesheet, with no CDN theme swap and no flash when data-theme changes.
nodes.languageNotes: A single .hljs rule set reads syntax colors from main.css custom properties, replacing a theme stylesheet that would otherwise be swapped at runtime.

nodes.name: workspace.css
nodes.summary: Styles the Documents, Research, and Code workspace panels, the My Documents side panel, the Settings dialog, and the text-size and density preferences. Panels are shown from html[data-workspace].

nodes.name: listSessions
nodes.summary: GET /sessions for a user id and returns the session list JSON.

nodes.name: createSession
nodes.summary: POST /sessions with a JSON body to create a chat session, forwarding an optional abort signal.

nodes.name: getSession
nodes.summary: GET /sessions/{sessionId} and returns that session's JSON.

nodes.name: updateSession
nodes.summary: PATCH /sessions/{sessionId} with a JSON body to update title, model, or other session fields.

nodes.name: deleteSession
nodes.summary: DELETE /sessions/{sessionId} to remove a chat session.

nodes.name: setFeedback
nodes.summary: POST /messages/{messageId}/feedback with a JSON value for thumbs feedback on an answer.

nodes.name: listDocuments
nodes.summary: GET /documents for a user id and returns the uploaded document list.

nodes.name: uploadFile
nodes.summary: POST /upload as multipart FormData for one file, scoped by user id.

nodes.name: uploadUrl
nodes.summary: POST /upload with a url query parameter so the backend ingests a remote page.

nodes.name: deleteDocument
nodes.summary: DELETE /documents/{docId} for a user id to remove one ingested document.

nodes.name: listGithubRepos
nodes.summary: GET /github/repos for a user id and returns connected repositories.

nodes.name: connectGithub
nodes.summary: POST /github/connect with a repository URL, optional token, and user id.

nodes.name: deleteGithubRepo
nodes.summary: DELETE /github/repos/{repoId} for a user id to disconnect a repository.

nodes.name: startGithubDevice
nodes.summary: POST /github/oauth/device to begin a GitHub device-code login.

nodes.name: pollGithubDevice
nodes.summary: POST /github/oauth/poll with the device code and user id until the login completes.

nodes.name: getHealth
nodes.summary: GET /health and returns read-only service status for the database, providers, and embeddings.

nodes.name: getConfig
nodes.summary: GET /config and returns advertised upload limits (max size and extensions).

nodes.name: getModels
nodes.summary: GET /models and returns the model catalog the composer can offer.

nodes.name: chatStream
nodes.summary: POST /chat/stream and reads the SSE body, dispatching meta, status, citations, model, token, artifact, error, and done events until the stream ends.

nodes.name: dispatch
nodes.summary: Parses one LF-delimited SSE block into an event name and JSON data, then invokes the matching own-property handler.

nodes.name: downloadArtifact
nodes.summary: GET /messages/{messageId}/download and starts a browser download using the Content-Disposition filename.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Boots theme, mode, and user id, loads models, sessions, documents, and config in parallel, then binds artifact download and DOM events.

nodes.name: _loadModels
nodes.summary: GET /models via API.getModels, keeps usable ids, persists the selection, and asks the UI to render the model select.

nodes.name: _bindEvents
nodes.summary: Wires send, stop, composer keys, mode and model changes, new chat, sidebar, file and URL upload, and the GitHub connect controls.

nodes.name: _startCooldown
nodes.summary: Starts a send cooldown from a Retry-After duration and announces when the user can send again.

nodes.name: _requestErrorMessage
nodes.summary: Turns a failed request error into the toast text shown for a send that never started.

nodes.name: _onSend
nodes.summary: Runs one chat turn: ensures a session, POSTs /chat/stream through API.chatStream, and maps SSE events onto the Chat renderer until done, stop, or error.

nodes.name: _retryAfterError
nodes.summary: Retries the last failed send after the server cooldown, using the regenerate path when the user turn was already stored.

nodes.name: _ensureSession
nodes.summary: Creates a session with API.createSession when the composer has no session id yet, and stores the returned id.

nodes.name: _newChat
nodes.summary: Clears the current transcript and session id so the next send starts a new conversation.

nodes.name: _selectSession
nodes.summary: Loads one session with API.getSession and renders its history in the transcript.

nodes.name: _deleteSession
nodes.summary: Confirms and DELETE /sessions via API.deleteSession, then refreshes the sidebar list.

nodes.name: _renameSession
nodes.summary: PATCH /sessions with a new title via API.updateSession and refreshes the session row.

nodes.name: _loadSessions
nodes.summary: GET /sessions via API.listSessions and stores the sidebar list, marking sessions as loaded.

nodes.name: _loadConfig
nodes.summary: GET /config via API.getConfig and stores the upload size and extension limits used by the composer.

nodes.name: _handleFiles
nodes.summary: Accepts the file input selection and starts an upload for each chosen file.

nodes.name: _handleFileUpload
nodes.summary: Builds an upload job that POSTs one file through API.uploadFile and runs it with the shared upload helper.

nodes.name: _onUrlSubmit
nodes.summary: Reads the URL modal and POSTs the address through API.uploadUrl as an ingest job.

nodes.name: _runUpload
nodes.summary: Runs one upload job, shows progress and success or the server error, then reloads the document list.

nodes.name: _deleteDocument
nodes.summary: Confirms and DELETE /documents via API.deleteDocument for a single row, then reloads the list.

nodes.name: _deleteSelectedDocuments
nodes.summary: Deletes every selected document id with API.deleteDocument and then reloads the list.

nodes.name: _loadDocuments
nodes.summary: GET /documents via API.listDocuments and stores the rows the document view renders.

nodes.name: _disconnectGithub
nodes.summary: DELETE /github/repos via API.deleteGithubRepo and refreshes the connected-repo list.

nodes.name: _onGithubSubmit
nodes.summary: POSTs a repository URL and optional token through API.connectGithub, then reloads connected repos.

nodes.name: _onGithubOauth
nodes.summary: Starts GitHub device login with API.startGithubDevice and polls API.pollGithubDevice until it completes or fails.

nodes.name: _setLoading
nodes.summary: Toggles the send and stop buttons and keeps focus on the composer while a stream is in flight.

nodes.name: _bindScroll
nodes.summary: Tracks whether the reader is near the bottom of the transcript so streaming auto-scroll can stick or release.

nodes.name: _buildAssistant
nodes.summary: Builds the assistant message shell: avatar, activity steps, Markdown body, sources, and action row.

nodes.name: _setNote
nodes.summary: Writes a status note on an assistant message, used for interruptions, partial answers, and artifact errors.

nodes.name: appendUserMessage
nodes.summary: Appends a user bubble to the transcript, hides the welcome screen, and scrolls to the new message.

nodes.name: startAssistantMessage
nodes.summary: Starts a live assistant message and returns the controller for thoughts, tokens, citations, badges, errors, and artifact cards.

nodes.name: copyMessage
nodes.summary: Copies the stored Markdown for a message to the clipboard and flashes the copy control.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md, the getting-started and architecture guide for this low-latency agentic RAG chatbot. It introduces the chat lifecycle, the HTTP API, configuration, testing, and the optional MCP server, which is the map for the rest of the tour. The later steps follow that map through the FastAPI process, hybrid retrieval, model failover, and the browser that streams the answer.

tour.title: Server Startup
tour.description: backend/main.py is the code entry the dependency walk starts from. It is a FastAPI application factory that configures CORS, mounts the single-page app, and owns container startup and shutdown. The Procfile starts one uvicorn worker on the platform-assigned port with backend.main:app, so a deployed process runs that same factory. Routes, settings, and the composition root are the first imports underneath it.
tour.languageLesson: A Procfile names process types for the host. Here the web process is one uvicorn worker pointed at the module path backend.main:app, which loads the FastAPI instance named app.

tour.title: Settings and Wiring
tour.description: Two modules directly under main.py decide what the process may know and how services are built. backend/core/config.py is the sole environment reader and the most imported backend module: Pydantic settings hold API keys, the free-tier model registry, RAG and rerank thresholds, and derived data paths. .env.example lists those keys and the defaults for models, embeddings, retrieval, search, history, and the HTTP server, and config.py is the module that reads them. backend/core/container.py constructs every service once, wires constructor dependencies, and exposes FastAPI Depends getters so the routes stay thin.
tour.languageLesson: A Pydantic settings model loads and validates environment variables in one place. The rest of the app receives a Settings object, so service code does not read the process environment itself.

tour.title: Layer Import Rules
tour.description: tests/test_architecture.py is the rule that makes the import direction predictable before you read the services. Imports may only point at allowed lower layers, module-level imports must be acyclic, and environment reads and model ids must stay in core.config. The enforced stack runs from utilities up through core, client, services, and the API to main. That is why the walk from main.py spreads downward: routes and the container fan out into services, and services reach clients and helpers.
tour.languageLesson: An architecture test imports the package graph and fails when a module reaches a forbidden layer. Keeping environment reads and model ids inside core.config means a new provider is a settings change rather than a string copied through the services.

tour.title: HTTP and MCP Doors
tour.description: backend/api/routes.py is the HTTP surface main.py mounts: thin handlers for chat streaming, sessions, uploads, GitHub, retrieval, and web search. POST /chat/stream is the route the browser uses, and it emits Server-Sent Events from the chat pipeline. POST /upload and POST /retrieve are the sibling doors for indexing a file or URL and for hybrid search with optional reranking. The optional stdio server in mcp_server.py exposes document search, web search, GitHub connect, and the same chat pipeline to MCP clients.

tour.title: Sessions and Schemas
tour.description: Those handlers accept and return the Pydantic schemas in backend/models/api.py, covering sessions, chat, uploads, retrieval, search, GitHub, and health. backend/models/db.py stores sessions, messages, documents, GitHub credentials, and repository briefs, and deleting a session cascades to its messages. backend/core/database.py owns the engine and session factory, creates tables, runs short transactions, and applies additive column migrations, while SessionService returns pydantic schemas so callers never hold ORM objects. security-issue-authz.md records an open gap: session read, rename, delete, and message feedback do not check ownership, because user_id is supplied by the client.
tour.languageLesson: Additive column migrations add columns the new code needs and leave existing rows in place. SessionService returns Pydantic schemas so a route never keeps a SQLAlchemy instance after the short transaction commits.

tour.title: The Chat Turn
tour.description: ChatService is the pipeline behind POST /chat/stream: it routes a turn, checks the semantic cache, retrieves documents and runs web search in parallel, then streams a model answer with failover while the session layer persists the turn. PromptBuilder gives every client the same prompt, with mode and specialist system text, numbered document and web context, and a token-budgeted history. The cache holds a bounded TTL LRU plus a per-scope cosine cache of earlier answers, so a repeated question can skip the model. sse.py encodes each pipeline event as one Server-Sent Events frame, and streaming.py strips think-style reasoning blocks even when the tags arrive in different chunks.
tour.languageLesson: An SSE frame carries an event name and a JSON data payload, so the browser can distinguish a token from a citation or an error. The think-tag filter keeps state across chunks, because a start tag and its end tag can land in different pieces of the stream.

tour.title: Hybrid Retrieval
tour.description: When ChatService retrieves, RetrievalService fuses FAISS cosine hits with FTS5 BM25 through reciprocal rank fusion, reranks the candidates, and gates them by relevance, falling back to lexical search or the fused order when the embedder or reranker is down. IndexStore persists that hybrid index: chunk text lives in SQLite with FTS5, per-user FAISS indexes are keyed by a hash of the user id, and rows and vectors commit together. EmbeddingService and RerankService load their models lazily, share a failure cooldown, and publish status so retrieval can degrade the turn. ranking.py merges the weighted ranked id lists that the fusion step consumes.

tour.title: Documents and Repositories
tour.description: The hybrid index is filled by DocumentService, which parses a file, URL, or raw text, chunks it, embeds it, and writes both the index and a document row. Parser converts PDF, Office, CSV, Excel, HTML, JSON, images, and plain text into page records of text plus metadata. GitHubService connects a repository, indexes selected source files into the same store, and keeps a per-user token plus an LLM-written repository brief, using a personal access token or the OAuth device flow. URL downloads go through an SSRF-safe web client that re-checks every redirect and rejects oversized bodies, and net.py allows only http(s) URLs whose resolved addresses are public.

tour.title: Web Search Policy
tour.description: In parallel with retrieval, SearchService applies the web-search policy ChatService calls: a TTL cache, a hard deadline, Tavily with a Serper fallback, and parallel sub-queries in research mode. The Tavily and Serper clients are async HTTP wrappers, each with a pooled client and one retry on transient failures. Those calls share the httpx AsyncClient from http.py, which takes its connect timeout from Settings and keeps a connection pool that outbound LLM calls reuse. The hits return as the numbered web context PromptBuilder places beside the document context.

tour.title: Model Failover
tour.description: Once the prompt is assembled, LLMService selects a model chain, fails over before the first token, and wraps each provider with a circuit breaker and a quota guard. That policy is what lets a free-tier Groq or Gemini failure switch models before any answer text is streamed. llm_client.py is the OpenAI-compatible transport for Groq and Google chat models: it opens streamed completions, lists model ids, and maps SDK failures onto normalised LLMError codes. The rate limiter adds a per-user token bucket and a per-model rolling quota so an exhausted free-tier model is skipped before it returns 429, and exceptions.py keeps client-facing messages free of upstream provider text.
tour.languageLesson: Failover runs before the first streamed token so the client receives one continuous answer. The circuit breaker stops calling a provider that is already failing, and the quota guard consults a local rolling window so the app can skip a model that would answer with HTTP 429.

tour.title: Browser Chat Shell
tour.description: The SPA mounted by main.py starts at frontend/index.html. An inline script sets theme, shell, and workspace before first paint, then the page loads local stylesheets and classic scripts, with app.js last. app.js owns browser state: it wires the composer, sessions, uploads, and GitHub controls, and it drives the single POST /chat/stream round trip through window.API and window.Chat. api.js wraps the JSON routes and opens the SSE channel plus artifact downloads, chat.js renders messages and citations without calling fetch, and utils.js sanitizes Markdown with DOMPurify before citation badges and highlight.js chrome are added.
tour.languageLesson: These are classic scripts that share behavior through window.API and window.Chat, loaded in order so app.js runs last. View code paints the DOM, and the controller plus api.js own the network. DOMPurify runs before citation and syntax-highlight markup is added, so streamed Markdown cannot inject HTML.

tour.title: Offline Test Harness
tour.description: pytest.ini collects tests from tests/, adds the project root to the path, and excludes live provider tests unless the live marker is selected, so a normal run stays offline. conftest.py supplies the fakes behind that run: a deterministic embedder and reranker, a scripted LLM provider, and a ServiceContainer factory that builds the FastAPI test client. test_api.py exercises every route, the SSE chat contract, uploads, search fallback, and rate limits. test_retrieval.py checks hybrid ingest and search, owner isolation, degraded embedder and reranker paths, and atomic index rollback, and test_llm.py covers failover, circuit-breaker trips, quota-guard skips, and think-block filtering.
tour.languageLesson: A pytest marker such as live separates tests that need real provider keys from the offline suite. Leaving that marker deselected in pytest.ini keeps an ordinary pytest run on the fakes from conftest.py.
